findings.summary: A code chord (viewport.frame = KeyF) also matches any physical key whose e.key is 'f', so F no longer means only the physical key as the old shortcutFor (code-only) did and as the README says
findings.scenario: Dvorak layout: the physical KeyY key types 'f'; pressing it in the viewport now frames the selection (before: nothing), so two keys frame instead of one

findings.summary: bind() accepts chord lists that KeymapOverridesPref's validator rejects (more than 8 chords), returns ok:true, then the pref subscriber sees the stored value without that action and setOverrides silently drops the binding
findings.scenario: keymap.bind('edit.undo', nine valid chords) returns {ok:true}; persist() stores overrides without edit.undo; the subscription re-applies them and edit.undo is back on its defaults in memory and on disk
